summary: Hungary: the 2013-2017 residency bond programme is well documented on the money side (ÁKK annual reports give bond series and stock: EUR 1.844 billion face value issued, all repaid by 2022; the laws are in the gazette), but official counts of people come only from one 2015 ministerial answer by nationality and from press reports of immigration-office data (about 6,500 investors and 13,300 family members); parliamentary answers are behind a CAPTCHA. Cost and intermediary profit figures are TI/KFIB estimates. The Guest Investor Program (Act XC of 2023, in force 2024) has clear rules (EUR 250,000 fund units, EUR 1m university donation; the EUR 500,000 property route was dropped on 30 Dec 2024) but no official statistics, only press figures showing very low take-up. Latvia: Latvia ran five-year investor residence permits from 1 Jul 2010 (property, company capital, bank subordinated liabilities, and from 2015 interest-free state bonds). The law history is fully documented from likumi.lv consolidated versions: thresholds rose from LVL 100,000/50,000 to EUR 250,000 plus a 5% state payment on 1 Sep 2014; Russians and Belarusians were excluded from 24 Sep 2022; the bond route was deleted on 20 May 2026 and the property and bank routes ended with the new Immigration Law on 15 Sep 2026. PMLP publishes first-time permits (2015 on) and valid-permit stocks by route, nationality and main applicant vs family member, which show the property route shrinking from about 5,000 main investors (2015) to about 1,000 (2026); there are no official figures on money invested or state payments collected.

observations.notes: Face value of settlement bonds outstanding at end-2016 (8 series). The same row gives HUF 402,086.66 million. Face value, not the cash the state received (bonds were sold at a discount).

observations.location: PDF p. 53, Függelék, table 'Letelepedési kötvény', row Összesen
observations.notes: Face value outstanding at end-2017, after the last issue (11 series). Series 2020/T shows EUR 336.10 million here but 336.60 million in the 2016 report.

observations.location: p. 6, 2. táblázat, row Total
observations.notes: Same figure as the ÁKK 2017 annual report, reproduced by TI/KFIB.

observations.location: PDF p. 20, Devizalejáratok
observations.quote: a Letelepedési Kötvény első sorozatának 107,5 millió eurós lejárata valósult meg 2018-ban
observations.notes: Face value repaid at maturity of series 2018/T. p. 26 of the same report puts it at HUF 35 billion.

observations.location: PDF p. 20, Devizalejáratok
observations.quote: a Letelepedési Magyar Államkötvények utolsó 3 sorozatának 555 millió eurós lejárata valósult meg 2022-ben
observations.notes: Final three series repaid in 2022; ÁKK says this ended the settlement bonds ('kifutottak a Letelepedési Kötvények').

observations.location: para 1
observations.quote: 2013 és 2016 között összesen 17 ezer 9 darab letelepedési kötvényt adott el
observations.notes: Ministry for National Economy answer to MP Sneider, as reported. Counts bond pieces, not investors: one EUR 250,000 bond per applicant in 2013-2014, but from 2015 five or six EUR 50,000 bonds per applicant, so it overstates the number of investors.

observations.location: p. 4, section 2
observations.quote: 6.621 kötvényt jegyeztek le
observations.notes: TI/KFIB do not give a source for this count. Read as the number of investor packages (one per applicant: EUR 250,000 to end-2014, EUR 300,000 from 2015). TI dates the programme's close to 30 June 2017; ÁKK says sales ended 31 March 2017.

observations.location: para 4
observations.quote: a közvetítő cégek 6570 ember után jegyeztek le letelepedési állampapírt
observations.notes: Persons for whom the intermediaries subscribed bonds, per Magyar Nemzet as relayed by Index; compared there with 6,585 investor settlement permits (BMH). The mismatch was not explained.

observations.quote: Az öt év alatt kumulált bevétel 1,666 milliárd eurót, vagy 514 milliárd forintot
observations.notes: Cash received by the state for bonds with EUR 1.844 billion face value (discount bonds). KFIB estimate assuming even sales within each series' window; also given as HUF 514 billion at quarterly exchange rates.

observations.location: p. 10, 4. táblázat, row 'Bevétel letelepedési kötvényekből'
observations.quote: Bevétel letelepedési kötvényekből 28,2 122,5 94,7 114,0 154,9 514,3
observations.notes: Estimated proceeds to the state from settlement bond sales, HUF billion. The table is labelled 'Forrás: ÁKK' but p. 7 explains that proceeds are KFIB estimates from ÁKK series data.

observations.location: p. 8, 3. táblázat, row Összesen
observations.quote: Összesen 1 844 66,4
observations.notes: Estimated extra cost to the state versus issuing ordinary five-year euro bonds at market yields (plus a 20bp fee): a gain in 2013-2014 and losses from 2015, net EUR 66.4 million (more than HUF 21 billion). Compared with EIB loans KFIB put the loss near HUF 30 billion.

observations.location: p. 3, Vezetői összefoglaló
observations.quote: Magyarország azonban 30 milliárd forintot bukott
observations.notes: Upper, rounded estimate that also compares the bonds with cheaper EIB loans; EIB loan rates are confidential, so this rests on assumptions (p. 3: 'konzervatív feltételezések mellett is megközelíti a 30 milliárd forintot').

observations.quote: a közvetítő cégek 60 milliárd forint magyar közpénzből származó nyereséget könyvelhettek el
observations.notes: Profit attributed to the intermediaries from the gap between the EUR 300,000 investors paid and the discounted price (about EUR 271,000) they paid ÁKK. Excludes the separate service fees charged to investors (Index reported EUR 45,000-60,000 per case).

observations.location: para 1
observations.quote: 6538 külföldi személy kapott letelepedési engedélyt befektetőként és további 47-en tartózkodási engedélyt
observations.notes: Investors (main applicants) who got a settlement permit, per BMH data released to Magyar Nemzet. A further 47 investors held only a residence permit.

observations.location: para 4
observations.quote: A BMH szerint például 6585 külföldi befektetői státuszban kapott letelepedési engedélyt
observations.notes: A second BMH figure quoted in the same article (from Magyar Nemzet), differing from the 6,538 in para 1; the article calls the data inconsistent.

observations.location: para 2
observations.quote: Családegyesítés alapján további 13 300 bevándorló kapott magyar letelepdési engedélyt
observations.notes: Family members with settlement permits through family reunification. BMH keeps no electronic record of family members who got only residence permits, so the true figure may be higher.

observations.location: para 3
observations.quote: A programban így összesen legalább 19 885 külföldi vett részt.
observations.notes: Total of investors and family members (6,538 + 47 + 13,300) as summed by Index/Magyar Nemzet; a minimum.

observations.location: p. 4, section 2
observations.quote: családtagokkal együtt, 19.855 külföldi állampolgár kapott magyar letelepedési engedélyt
observations.notes: Investors plus family members with settlement permits; no source given. Differs slightly from the 19,885 (Index) and 19,838 (444) totals.

observations.location: final paragraphs
observations.quote: Összesen 19,838 külföldi élt ezzel a lehetőséggel
observations.notes: Investors plus family members; no source given in the article.

observations.location: para after Kontrát's answer
observations.quote: mindössze 16 személy (5 befektető és 11 családtag) letelepedési engedélyét vonták vissza utólag
observations.notes: Settlement permits withdrawn afterwards from bond-programme participants: 5 investors and 11 family members. BMH data obtained by Direkt36. None of the Russians named in press investigations were among them, per 444.

program_terms.notes: Translation: 'holds securities of at least EUR 250,000 face value, with a term of at least five years, issued by an undertaking' that itself buys special zero-coupon Hungarian government bonds of EUR 250,000 (discount rate 1.5 points below the market yield, at least 2%). program_terms.notes: Applies to applications filed after 1 Jan 2015 under s. 110(11) of Act II of 2007; bonds now in EUR 50,000 pieces (six per applicant). programs.name: Hungarian residency bond programme (Letelepedési Magyar Államkötvény, settlement bond)
programs.notes: Residence permit in the 'national economic interest' under s. 28(3)-(11) of Act II of 2007 (added by Act CCXX of 2012) for holders of at least EUR 250,000 (EUR 300,000 from 2015) of five-year securities sold by private intermediaries approved by Parliament's economic committee (eight in all, mostly offshore; one per country); the intermediaries bought discounted zero-coupon euro bonds from ÁKK. Settlement (permanent residence) permit after six months, directly from July 2016 per Index. ÁKK: EUR 1.844 billion face value issued 2013-2017 in 11 series, all repaid by 2022. BMH: about 6,500 investors and 13,300 family members. Residence route only; normal naturalisation rules applied.

programs.name: Hungarian Guest Investor Program (vendégbefektetői vízum és tartózkodási engedély)
programs.notes: Act XC of 2023, ss. 16 and 22: six-month guest investor visa, then a 10-year residence permit renewable for 10 more, with the right to work. Routes: EUR 250,000 in units of a qualified Hungarian real estate fund held 5 years; EUR 1,000,000 donation to a foundation-run university; EUR 500,000 residential property until removed on 30 Dec 2024. Security vetting by the Constitution Protection Office; fund managers need clearance. Law in force 1 Jan 2024, but the first fund manager qualified only in Oct 2024. No official statistics are published; press reports from OIF data show very low take-up.

programs.name: Latvia temporary residence permits for investors (Imigrācijas likums, 23. panta pirmās daļas 28.-31. punkts)
programs.notes: Five-year renewable temporary residence permits (termiņuzturēšanās atļauja, TUA) for investors and their spouses and minor children, under art. 23(1) points 28 (company capital), 29 (real estate), 30 (subordinated liabilities with a Latvian bank) and 31 (interest-free state securities, 2015 to May 2026) of the 2002 Immigration Law; added by the law of 22.04.2010, in force 1 Jul 2010. Run by the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP). Russian and Belarusian citizens excluded from 24 Sep 2022. The state-securities route was deleted from 20 May 2026; the property and bank routes ended when the new Immigration Law took effect on 15 Sep 2026, which keeps a two-year business-investment permit and adds an (not yet operational) EUR 150,000 state fund route, so the programme continues in reduced form. Under art. 24(1) point 7 of the 2002 law, a foreigner who has lived in Latvia continuously with a temporary residence permit for at least five years may request permanent residence (other conditions, such as language, apply; not detailed here). Citizenship rules not researched.

Latvia: No official figures on the amount invested (property value, bank placements, bonds bought) or on the state-budget payments collected (5% property payment, EUR 10,000/25,000/38,000 payments, EUR 5,000 renewal payments). PMLP and the Cabinet prepared informative reports on the implementation of art. 23(1) points 3, 28-31 (mentioned in PMLP annual reports 2014, 2015 and 2018) that analyse investment and budget effects, but they were not located.

Latvia: No PMLP statistics found for 2010-2013 by investor route (annual reports only give overall permit totals; the 2014 report gives 4,982 first-time permits for property purchase in 2014 and the 2015 report 1,145 for 2015). Online statistics tables start in 2015.
Latvia: Renewals (atkārtotas TUA) by investor route are not published; only first-time permits and valid stocks. First-time tables count only persons with no earlier residence permit of any kind.

Latvia: First-time permit PDFs for 2015-2020 have unlabelled rows in the investor column block, so nationality splits for those years were not extracted (only all-country totals). The 31.12.2020 valid-permit PDF also lacks country names in that block. Nationality rows for valid stocks are included only for selected nationalities with at least 20 main-applicant permits (first-time: at least 5).

Latvia: Breakdown column: nationality rows use a compound breakdown "route=...;nationality=..." because PMLP splits by both; the data model allows one split, so the merge may need to handle this (e.g. separate indicators).
Latvia: Outcome of the Financial Intelligence Unit review of investor permits held by Russian and Belarusian citizens (deadline 1 Oct 2023) not found; number of annulled permits unknown.
Latvia: No Saeima, State Audit Office (Valsts kontrole) or European Commission (COM(2019)12) material was read in this pass; web search budget was exhausted mid-task.

Latvia: A 2024 draft amendment (tapportals 24-TA-3000) proposed raising the property threshold to EUR 350,000; it was apparently not adopted (the final 2002-law text keeps EUR 250,000), but its fate was not traced.
Latvia: Applications received/approved/rejected by route are not published apart from the 2,532 (2014) and 398 (2015) investor-application totals.
